title: Heavenly Eye Trial
next_chapter_hook: The independent will of the 49th chess piece is finally confirmed in the illusion, the core of the Heavenly Eye slowly opens, what awaits Chen Ji is the ultimate truth sealed ten thousand years ago.

text.content: The moment Chen Ji stepped into the core of the Heavenly Eye, he felt the lament of a chess game from ten thousand years ago—the silent cry of one abandoned by Heavenly Will. The void around him was like torn silk, countless threads of destiny weaving into an enormous chess web, and he stood at the center of the board. Some threads were thick as arms, emanating the aura of ancient sects; others were fine as strands of hair, connecting the rise and fall of common folk. And all threads ultimately converged toward one direction—that unopened golden vertical pupil.

Chen Ji steadied his mind. The Tianji Record Fragment in his consciousness grew slightly warm, but no warning came. He sneered in his heart: Is this the Heavenly Eye's way of receiving guests? Silently dragging people into an illusion without even a word of introduction. He looked around and found himself standing on a floating circular stone platform, covered with densely packed runes, each rune telling a story that had already ended. Some protagonists of those stories were full of vigor, some lingered on desperately, but their endings were all the same—death.

"You've arrived." An aged yet majestic voice came from all directions, as if heaven and earth themselves were speaking. Chen Ji did not respond, merely standing quietly at the center of the stone platform, hands clasped behind his back, his expression betraying no emotion. The voice continued: "Over ten thousand years, you are the 49th prophet to step into this place." Before the words finished, the runes on the stone platform blazed brightly, and 49 pillars of light shot up around Chen Ji. Within those pillars appeared 49 vague silhouettes—some in splendid robes, some in ragged garments, some in their prime, some already in their twilight years. But they all shared one thing: a golden vertical pupil at their brow center, identical to the Heavenly Eye.

dialogue.content: "They were all inheritors of the Tianji Record, standing in the same position as you, facing the same choices." The Heavenly Eye's voice carried an imperceptible mockery. "Yet they all failed. Their deaths varied—some died of greed, some of benevolence, some of passion, some of arrogance. But ultimately, they all died for the same reason: they thought they were the chess players." The figures in the light pillars began rapidly playing their life scenes. Chen Ji watched as Prophet Number 1 was jointly executed by three major sects for exposing Heavenly Secrets; Prophet Number 17 triggered an even greater catastrophe by trying to change a great war; Prophet Number 33 surrendered the Tianji Record for love... Every story was filled with irony, every failure precisely hitting the weakness of human nature.

text.content: Chen Ji remained silent, but as his gaze swept over those light pillars, something churned in the depths of his eyes. Forty-nine versions of himself—some confident, some timid, some indecisive, some stubborn. They were all dead, dying on the path of thinking they could control destiny. And now, what the Heavenly Eye wanted him to see was merely a conclusion: you are merely the 49th destined-to-fail chess piece. Yet another voice whispered in Chen Ji's heart: since you all failed, that can only mean one thing—your chess game wasn't big enough.

The illusion began to change. The 49 light pillars suddenly vanished, replaced by a vast boundless starry sky. Every star was a thread of destiny, and Chen Ji stood at the very center of this sea of stars. "Chen Ji," the Heavenly Eye's voice sounded again, this time with a bit more seriousness, "you have three hours to think. After three hours, you will face a choice—accept the complete inheritance of the Tianji Record and become my spokesperson; or refuse, and be erased by destiny from that moment on." The stars in the sky began spinning madly, countless images flashing before Chen Ji's eyes like a carousel: Su Qingyao collapsed in a pool of blood, Ye Qing chased by the Holy Sect to a desperate end, Chen Nian imprisoned in darkness by chains... "These are possible futures that may occur," the Heavenly Eye's voice bewitched, "and I can help you change them."

Chen Ji suddenly laughed. That laughter echoed particularly harshly in the empty starry sea. "Change the future?" He finally spoke, his voice calm as if he weren't discussing his own life and death. "If I wanted to change the future, why would I need to rely on others?" The Heavenly Eye seemingly hadn't expected such a response. The spinning stars halted for an instant. "You're joking," the Heavenly Eye's voice cooled. "You think the Tianji Record Fragment gave you some extraordinary ability? Foreseeing three hours? How可笑. You can't even calculate who will assassinate you at noon tomorrow, yet you presume to oppose destiny?" Chen Ji unhurriedly took out the Tianji Record Fragment from his chest. That yellowed page radiated a faint glow in the starry sea, forming a subtle confrontation with the surrounding Heavenly Power. "Can't calculate?" He unfolded the fragment. "Then let me show you how I calculate."

dialogue.content: The Heavenly Secrets runes on the fragment began flashing frantically. Chen Ji injected all his Heavenly Fate Value into it—that was a full five points, enough to foresee the scene three hours later. However, this time, what he saw was not a vague future fragment, but a clear image: the Heavenly Eye's true purpose. "So that's how it is," after Chen Ji finished viewing, a cold smile curved his lips. "You want me to become the 50th manipulated chess piece, not for any bullshit spokesperson, but to use my Tianji Record to fill your consumption from that battle ten thousand years ago." The starry sea froze instantly. The Heavenly Eye's golden vertical pupil finally slowly opened one in the void, its icy gaze fixed directly on Chen Ji. "You're very clever," its voice carried a hint of killing intent. "Clever people often die the fastest."

text.content: Chen Ji retracted the fragment into his chest. Facing that golden vertical pupil's gaze, he did not retreat but advanced instead. "If I feared death, I wouldn't have stepped in here." He surveyed the gradually freezing starry sea around him. "As for you, Heavenly Eye—you were gravely wounded by a prophet ten thousand years ago, hiding in the core area licking your wounds for ten thousand years. Now that you've finally found a usable chess piece, you don't even have the basic sincerity." His voice wasn't loud, yet it was like a blade stabbing into the void. "Where are the promised trials? Where is the promised choice? I thought the Heavenly Will would be so lofty, but turns out you're just some low-life scheme pushing chess pieces around."

choice.prompt: Chen Ji saw through the Heavenly Eye's true purpose. Facing this terrifying existence that had slept for ten thousand years, he decided—

choices.description: Directly challenge the Heavenly Eye's authority, tear apart its lofty mask with words, displaying the true colors of "sharp-tongued humiliation."
choices.visible_reward: See through the illusion's true nature, obtain crucial intelligence
choices.risk_hint: May trigger combat by provoking the Heavenly Eye

text.content: The Heavenly Eye's golden vertical pupil contracted sharply. It clearly hadn't expected a mere Golden Core stage废物 to dare be so presumptuous. "Presumptuous!" True anger entered its voice, and countless golden thunderbolts descended from the starry sea, each capable of turning an ordinary Nascent Soul cultivator to ash. Yet Chen Ji stood motionless, letting those thunderbolts dissipate three feet before him—it wasn't that he was so powerful, but a dark barrier manifested on the Tianji Record Fragment, firmly protecting him. Mo Xiansheng's voice wafted out from the fragment: "What's the rush? Its injuries from ten thousand years ago remain unrecovered. It's merely bluffing."

Upon hearing this, Chen Ji's smile grew even wider. "So even after ten thousand years, the wounds still haven't healed?" He stepped forward, staring directly at that golden vertical pupil. "Then let me see how many prophets this half-dead appearance of yours can still frighten?" His words were like knives cutting into the Heavenly Eye's wounds. "Forty-nine chess pieces, you've used them forty-nine times, and failed every time—not because the chess pieces weren't good enough, but because the choices you gave them were dead ends from the start."

choices.description: 表面上 accept the trial, while secretly searching for cracks in the illusion, using the method of "playing the pig to eat the tiger" to wait for the counterattack opportunity.
choices.visible_reward: Obtain more information about the Heavenly Eye
choices.risk_hint: May be seen as weak and despised

text.content: Chen Ji收敛 his smile, lowered his eyelids, assuming a thoughtful expression. "What Your Heavenly Highness says is extremely wise. The junior was presumptuous just now." His tone became respectful, as if truly intimidated by the Heavenly Eye's power. The golden thunderbolts in the starry sea quietly dissipated. A satisfied glint flashed in the Heavenly Eye's vertical pupil. "A wise man knows when to bow to circumstances," it slowly said. "You are smarter than all forty-nine predecessors." Chen Ji kept his head lowered, yet a curve at the corner of his lips that no one else could see—he could see it: the more satisfied it was, the more flaws it would reveal.

The illusion continued to evolve, and forty-nine pillars of light appeared once more. This time, instead of the failed prophets, the pillars manifested the forty-nine possible futures Chen Ji might walk: becoming a puppet of Heavenly Dao, dying a violent death, going mad into the Demonic Path, or leaving a stench for ten thousand generations... Each future came with detailed "chains of karma," as if telling him: no matter what you choose, the ending is fated. Chen Ji watched those pillars, and the light in his eyes grew brighter and brighter—the more detailed it displayed, the more rules it exposed.

choices.description: Activate Mo Xiansheng's power, utilizing the knowledge of this former guardian of the Tianji Record to break the illusion's cognitive limitations.
choices.visible_cost: Consume Mo Xiansheng's Residual Soul Power
choices.visible_reward: Obtain key information about the weaknesses of the Eye of Heavenly Dao
choices.risk_hint: Mo Xiansheng's power is limited, excessive use may endanger the residual soul's existence

text.content: Chen Ji quietly infused a thread of Heavenly Fate into the fragment, whispering: "Master Mo, your disciple seeks your guidance." The ink patterns on the fragment suddenly lit up, and Mo Xiansheng's phantom slowly emerged from the paper—a venerable old man with sharp, piercing eyes. "I have waited long for you to call upon me." Mo Xiansheng stroked his non-existent beard, his gaze sweeping across the surrounding star sea, "This illusion seems flawless, but it has one fatal flaw—it can only use past information to construct the future, while the true power of the Tianji Record is to create new possibilities that never existed in the past."

Upon hearing this, a brilliant light flashed in Chen Ji's eyes. "Creating new possibilities that never existed in the past..." he repeated softly, then suddenly burst into laughter, "So that's it! It showed me forty-nine failures, forty-nine futures, all based on causal chains that have already occurred—but what if I do something entirely beyond its comprehension?" Mo Xiansheng nodded, his phantom beginning to blur, "Go, show it in your own way what it means to have foresight in everything. Remember, I can only help you so much; the real chess game must be played by yourself."

The star sea shook violently, and the golden vertical pupil of the Eye of Heavenly Dao suddenly contracted into a thin line. That was no longer a cold scrutiny, but genuine wariness. "What are you doing?" its voice carried a hint of uncertainty, "You're merely a Foundation Building insect, how could you see through the nature of this illusion?" Chen Ji did not answer, only raising his right hand, palm facing upward, five fingers slightly spread. In the next second, something诡异 occurred—the fate threads originally controlled by the Eye of Heavenly Dao began snapping on their own, as if cut by invisible blades. Each broken thread transformed into scattered starlight, flowing into Chen Ji's palm.

"Impossible!" The Eye of Heavenly Dao's voice carried panic for the first time, "This is my domain, how could you—" Yet facts left no room for disbelief. As more and more fate threads were severed, cracks began appearing in the illusion. The seemingly impenetrable star sea barriers were covered with spider-web-like fissures. "You forgot one thing," Chen Ji's voice was calm and cold, "the Tianji Record Fragment existed before you. You used it to select your chess pieces, but forgot it can also reversely absorb the karma you weave." He clenched his fist, the starlight in his palm condensing into a small星辰, "You said I couldn't calculate who would assassinate me tomorrow at noon? Then let me show you how I dismantle the web you've been weaving for ten thousand years in one breath."

The illusion's cracks grew larger, the star sea began collapsing inward, countless stars exploding one after another like dominoes. The Eye of Heavenly Dao's golden vertical pupil flickered chaotically in the turmoil, its voice becoming increasingly ethereal. "Stop! You don't know what you're doing!" For the first time, its tone carried a pleading quality, "Without me, you cannot survive in this world! Those who covet the Tianji Record—the Three Great Sects, the Holy Sect of the Demonic Path, and even older existences—they will tear you to pieces within three days!" Hearing this, Chen Ji's lips curved into an even deeper cold smile. "Three days?" He took out a Jade Slip from his chest, "Then let me show you how I trap them all in a deadly game within three days."

choice.prompt: The illusion is about to collapse, and Chen Ji is about to gain access to the Eye of Heavenly Dao's core—this is the decisive moment, he chooses—

choices.description: Seize the moment when the Eye of Heavenly Dao is weakened, devour it completely, and use its power to fill the gaps in the Tianji Record, pursuing absolute power.
choices.visible_cost: May be counterattacked by Heavenly Dao's power
choices.visible_reward: Obtain partial abilities of the Eye of Heavenly Dao, Tianji Record upgraded
choices.risk_hint: Darkness value increases dramatically, may lose part of humanity

text.content: Chen Ji abruptly stepped forward, his right hand probing directly into the golden vertical pupil of the Eye of Heavenly Dao. It was a strange sensation—he seemed to touch ten thousand years of time, endless karma, and that lofty意志. The Eye of Heavenly Dao let out a凄厉 wail, its massive consciousness rapidly shrinking, while Chen Ji's Tianji Record Fragment frantically devoured the power it spilled. "You're mad!" the Eye of Heavenly Dao's voice carried despair, "Devouring me, you won't be able to withstand ten thousand years of karma—"

"Ten thousand years of karma?" Chen Ji冷笑, the suction in his palm growing even stronger, "The deficit you couldn't fill with forty-nine prophets, let me settle for you now." As the Eye of Heavenly Dao's consciousness grew smaller and smaller, Chen Ji felt a majestic power flooding into his body. The runes on the Tianji Record Fragment began rearranging, a completely new page slowly emerging. However, just then, an image flashed through his mind—Chen Nian's blurred silhouette, and a faint whisper: "Brother, don't..." His hand trembled slightly.

choices.description: Preserve the existence of the Eye of Heavenly Dao, domesticate it as part of the Tianji Record, leaving a key piece for future schemes.
choices.visible_cost: Must constantly guard against the Eye of Heavenly Dao's possible counterattack
choices.visible_reward: Obtain a powerful informant who can monitor the world's fate
choices.risk_hint: The Eye of Heavenly Dao may act one way while scheming another

text.content: Chen Ji withdrew his right hand, his five fingers gently flicking. An ink-colored restriction rune vanished into the Eye of Heavenly Dao's vertical pupil. The golden pupil trembled violently, then slowly closed. When it opened again, it already carried a hint of Chen Ji's气息. "From this day forward, you are the Seventeenth Page of the Tianji Record." Chen Ji's voice was calm yet left no room for doubt, "I shall give you a new name—Tianji Mirror. From now on, you need only do one thing: monitor all changes related to Heavenly Secrets under heaven for me. Any stirring, report to me immediately."

Although the consciousness of the Heavenly Eye was unwilling, it had no choice but to accept this unchangeable reality. The chess game it had laid over ten thousand years had now become the very cage imprisoning itself. "...As you command." Its voice carried humiliation, yet also a trace of relief. The ten thousand years of waiting had finally reached a conclusion, though this result was entirely different from what it had anticipated. Chen Ji nodded, and another star凝聚ed in his palm—the fate threads he had absorbed from the illusion, transformed into a star containing extraordinarily pure heavenly power. He pressed the star into the fragment, and at the previously incomplete seventeenth blank page, dense text began to slowly emerge.

choices.description: "Do not covet immediate gains, maintain independent will and judgment, and be bound by no power."
choices.visible_cost: "Miss the opportunity to strengthen one's power."
choices.visible_reward: "Remain clear-headed, possibly gaining the Heavenly Eye's favor."
choices.risk_hint: "May be viewed by the Heavenly Eye as weak and easily bullied."

text.content: Chen Ji slowly drew back his hand, stepping back several paces, maintaining a precarious distance from the Heavenly Eye. "I won't kill you," he said calmly, "nor do I need you to submit to me." A flicker of confusion passed through the golden vertical pupil of the Heavenly Eye. "You don't want to devour me, nor do you wish to control me? What exactly do you want?" Chen Ji smiled faintly, that smile carrying an indefinable nuance. "What I want has never required taking by force." He turned, his back to the Heavenly Eye. "You and I were never enemies—at least not now. You have your mission, and I have my path to walk. Consider this encounter as mutual sparring. Farewell."

The illusion began to collapse completely, stars extinguished one by one, the star sea dissolved into countless fragments. However, just as Chen Ji was about to leave the illusion, the Heavenly Eye's voice rang out once more—this time neither majestic nor angry, but carrying an indescribable complexity. "Wait." The golden vertical pupil slowly opened, reflecting a blurry silhouette—a woman's outline, bearing a seventy to eighty percent resemblance to Chen Nian, yet radiating an entirely different temperament. "This is the final testament left by the Prophet who abandoned me ten thousand years ago," the Heavenly Eye said. "She said that if any descendant could reach this place, this information should be passed to them—the complete form of the Tianji Record does not exist in this world."

Chen Ji's footsteps abruptly stopped. "Not in this world?" He turned, his gaze firmly fixed on that silhouette. A complex light flickered in the vertical pupil of the Heavenly Eye. "That Prophet exhausted her life pursuing the ultimate mysteries of the Tianji Record, eventually discovering that the true本体 of the Tianji Record was sealed in—" It paused, as if enduring some immense pressure. "The Heavenly Battlefield." At these three words, Chen Ji felt the Tianji Record fragment in his body suddenly surge with violent tremors—an unprecedented intense resonance. Mr. Mo's voice echoed in his mind: "The Heavenly Battlefield... The legendary end point of the ancient races' great war, where even the Heavenly Dao itself fell. If the本体 of the Tianji Record truly lies there..."

"Where is the Heavenly Battlefield?" Chen Ji asked in a deep voice, his tone carrying unprecedented urgency. The Heavenly Eye fell silent for a moment. "I don't know the exact location, but I know the method to open it." Its voice grew low. "Three things are needed: the blood essence of a Heavenly Fate bearer, the Tianji Record fragment, and—" Its vertical pupil abruptly contracted into a thin line. "The Heavenly Fate Key." Chen Ji's pupils tightened sharply. The Heavenly Fate Key—that was the title the Holy Sect gave Chen Nian when she was taken. His fists slowly clenched, his knuckles turning white. "You'd better pray," his voice was terrifyingly calm, "that what you're about to say justifies your ten thousand years of waiting."

The Heavenly Eye seemed intimidated by his aura, its voice lowering: "The Heavenly Fate Key is the only key to opening the Heavenly Battlefield. Her bloodline has some mysterious connection to the Tianji Record—that is why the Holy Sect spared no effort to obtain her." Chen Ji said nothing, but deep in his eyes, cold flames had already ignited. The Holy Sect... Chen Nian... The Heavenly Battlefield... The connection between these three was far tighter than he had imagined. He took a deep breath, forcibly pressing this information into his heart. "What else?" he asked. "Since you know these things, it means the Prophet from ten thousand years ago left more than just this."

A flicker of approval passed through the vertical pupil of the Heavenly Eye—though it had just been forced to this state by Chen Ji, this approval was genuine. "You're very clever." It slowly said. "Before the death of that Prophet ten thousand years ago, she sealed a portion of her memories within the Tianji Record fragment—the one in your hand. She hoped that a future inheritor could unlock these memories at a crucial moment and find the path she was unable to complete." Chen Ji lowered his gaze to the fragment in his hand, indeed discovering an extremely faint pattern along the edge of the page—one that would be unnoticeable without careful observation. He gently touched that pattern with his Heavenly Fate Value, and a blurry scene flooded his mind: a white-robed woman standing beneath a blood-red sky, behind her countless fallen bodies, and before her, a golden vertical pupil that blotted out the heavens.

choice.prompt: After unlocking part of the Prophet's memories from ten thousand years ago, Chen Ji, facing the road ahead, decided—

choices.description: Take finding his sister as the top priority, utilize all resources to investigate the Holy Sect's movements.
choices.visible_reward: Faster in finding clues about Chen Nian.
choices.risk_hint: May expose strength and attract powerful enemies.

text.content: Chen Ji put away the fragment and turned to leave the illusion. "Wait." The Heavenly Eye called out to him. "You're going to the Holy Sect now? At your current strength, you'd be crushed to pulp before even reaching their mountain gate." Chen Ji didn't look back. "That's not your concern." His voice was calm yet carried undeniable resolve. "My sister's matter cannot wait a single moment longer." The Heavenly Eye fell silent for a beat. "At least take this." A streak of golden light shot from its vertical pupil and entered Chen Ji's brow center—a crude map marking three outer guard posts of the Holy Sect and a possible tunnel leading to the interior. "This is intelligence I left behind ten thousand years ago; most of it is now outdated, but it's better than nothing."

Chen Ji slightly nodded, accepting this "kindness" in a sense. "You're quite sensible." He said coolly. "Rest assured, if I find Chen Nian, I'll return to set you free." Upon hearing this, a complex light flickered in the vertical pupil of the Heavenly Eye, but it said nothing. The exit of the illusion slowly opened before Chen Ji, revealing a dim void. He took a deep breath and stepped into it—the next step would be the Holy Sect, would be Chen Nian, would be the storm destined to sweep across the world.

choices.text: First return to Tianqing Sect to make arrangements.
choices.description: No need to rush; first return to the sect to consolidate foundations, secretly laying a chess game against the Holy Sect.
choices.visible_cost: Need to wait for the right moment.
choices.visible_reward: More thorough preparation, greater chance of victory.
choices.risk_hint: Chen Nian may suffer more torment during this period.

text.content: Chen Ji stopped and turned around, facing the Eye of Heavenly Dao once more. "You're right." His voice regained its calm. "The Holy Sect isn't something I can confront head-on right now, but I can make them tear themselves apart." A cold smile curled at the corner of his mouth as his mind began to race: Ye Qing's Demonic Path Holy Sect was a variable, Ling Yuan's secret dealings with the Holy Sect were leverage, and the tangled interests between the three great sects were pieces to be exploited. "Chen Nian..." he murmured silently in his heart, "Wait for me a little longer. I will definitely come for you."

The exit of the illusion gradually opened before Chen Ji, with faint rays of light penetrating the dim void. He cast one final glance at the Eye of Heavenly Dao, its golden vertical pupil growing increasingly intricate in the fading luminescence. "Remember your words today," the Eye of Heavenly Dao murmured, "Next time we meet, you'll either ascend to godhood or turn to ashes." Chen Ji offered no response, merely lifting the corner of his lips—a slight smile. He had grown accustomed to such threats. After all, in his perspective, nothing was beyond calculation. Stepping into the radiance, the illusion collapsed entirely, and his new game of chess was just beginning.

When Chen Ji opened his eyes again, he stood at the entrance of the core area of the Eye of Heavenly Dao. The eerie golden sea of light still surrounded him, yet its previous oppressive force had vanished. The Tianji Record Fragment rested quietly against his chest, with a faint golden line now appearing on the seventeenth page: Tianji Mirror - Subjugated. Chen Ji gazed down at his own hands, sensing that the threads of fate he had absorbed during the illusion had completely merged into his meridians. Though they hadn't dramatically elevated his combat power, they had deepened his comprehension of causal forces. "So this is the power of the Eye of Heavenly Dao..." he murmured, "merely a higher-dimensional weaving of causality."

Just then, a familiar voice came from behind him. "You're out." Chen Ji turned to see Su Qingyao standing not far away, gazing at him with a complex expression. Her white robes were stained with several drops of blood, clearly indicating that some battle had occurred during his time in the core area. "You're injured?" Chen Ji frowned, his eyes scanning the bloodstains. Su Qingyao shook her head. "Not me. Those are the Xuanwu Sect disciples who tried to force their way into the core area." Her voice was calm, but there was a hint of exhaustion deep in her eyes. "Han Lie didn't act personally, but he sent three waves of people to test us. You were inside for a full two hours, and outside has already fallen into chaos."

Upon hearing this, Chen Ji's frown deepened. Han Lie... that rival with a simple mind but逆天 combat power had chosen to watch and wait during his weakest moment instead of striking directly. What did that mean? It meant Han Lie was also wary of something, or rather, someone was guiding him from behind. "Where is Ling Yuan?" he asked. Su Qingyao's expression flickered slightly. "The old sect master left shortly after you entered the core area, saying he was going to 'handle some old matters.'" Her voice dropped lower. "I thought he left too hastily, as if... he was avoiding something." Chen Ji didn't speak, but a cold light had already flashed across his eyes. Ling Yuan, you better pray that what you're doing is worthy of your ten-thousand-year plan.

dialogue.content: Su Qingyao stepped closer, her gaze locked tightly on Chen Ji's eyes, as if trying to discern something from them. "What happened inside?" she asked. "What did you obtain?" Chen Ji met her gaze,沉默了片刻，然后轻轻摇了摇头。"Now is not the time." His voice was calm but carried undeniable resolve. "But I can tell you one thing—the trial of the Eye of Heavenly Dao, I've passed it." Su Qingyao's pupils contracted sharply; she was clearly shocked by the weight of these words. Countless geniuses had fallen over ten thousand years on this trial, yet this servant disciple who was called a废物 had actually passed it? She opened her mouth, wanting to ask more, but ultimately could only sigh softly. "I knew it," she said, "From the very beginning, I knew you were no ordinary废物."

text.content: Chen Ji looked at Su Qingyao and suddenly revealed a faint smile. "Does it matter if you know?" His voice carried a hint of playfulness. "Are you planning to tell the whole sect? Tell Ling Yuan? Tell Han Lie?" Su Qingyao snorted coldly. "If I wanted to speak, you would have died at least ten times by now." Chen Ji nodded. "That is the truth." The two stared at each other for a moment, and a subtle understanding filled the air. Su Qingyao finally looked away. "What are you planning to do next?" Chen Ji turned, gazing at the golden gate slowly opening in the depths of the core area. "Go back first." He said. "Some things need careful deliberation, and some accounts... are time to settle." His voice was calm, but Su Qingyao could hear the icy killing intent beneath it. She knew that the boy who had been viewed as a chess piece by the entire world was finally about to start placing his pieces.
